intent: Change wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m to raise yaw per unit of steering command, targeting the s-bend drift at max_error 0.0609. Keep the five-sensor row at y=0.08 spanning x=±0.06, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.03 m wheels, body 0.12 by 0.18 m and mass 0.7 kg, so this race isolates the turn-rate change. Expected: s-bend max_error at or below 0.06 m with fewer off-track exits, and oval finish rate at or above 0.85.
learning: Iteration 4 showed the s-bend fails by drift (max_error 0.0609, line loss 0.10), so the limit is turn rate rather than sensor reach. Iteration 4 also showed that the oval finish rate depends on controller authority (0.95 falling to 0.85 with the same geometry). Ask the Integrator: on the s-bend, does the robot exit on the first or second bend, and does the yaw rate saturate at the new track width? On the slalom, do the outer sensors read near zero at the line loss? Use the answers to choose between sensor_size 0.016 for the slalom and a return to wheel_track 0.12 if the narrower track causes oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 4 held the geometry at iteration 3's values, so its result isolates the controller change. The oval finish rate fell from 0.95 to 0.85 and the score fell from 340.07 to 319.08, but max_error on the oval stayed low (0.036) and the s-bend still left the track on all 20 runs at max_error 0.0609 with only 0.10 line-loss events per run. The s-bend failure is therefore a drift past the 0.06 m limit with the line still held, not a lost line. That is the condition the Integrator's rule names for a turn-rate limit: the robot cannot yaw fast enough per unit of steering command. Body changes cannot widen the limit, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body_width. Following that rule, I narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. The turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so the same steering command gives about 20 percent more yaw. I hold sensor_size at 0.012 and the sensor row at iteration 3's values, so the s-bend result isolates the track change. The slalom line loss (1.0 per run, progress 0.10) is a separate limit; I do not change sensor_size in the same race, because that would confound the s-bend result and the outer-sensor readings have not been reported. The oval finish-rate drop is probably a controller authority issue, which the Integrator is handling, so it is not a geometry change. Expected result: s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m or the s-bend progress rises above 0.17, and the oval finish rate holds at or above 0.85. If the s-bend still exits at about 0.061 m, the next step is sensor_size 0.016 for the slalom coverage problem.
